To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fore-stomach of the pouch young of tammar wallaby develops via two temporally discrete phases: down-regulation (or loss) of gastric glandular cells and initiation of cardiac glandular cells.
fore-stomachs of tammar wallaby pouch young cross-fostered into host mothers at later stages of lactational development display a reduced parietal cell and increased apoptotic cell population.

cross-fostering of pouch young (PY, the neonatal form of the tammar) to host mothers at later stages of lactational milk production accelerates development of the fore-stomach and that milk from later lactation stages and/or herbage consumption play a key role in this process.

the mechanisms that regulate the transition from gastric to cardia gland phenotype in tammar PY fore-stomachs.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fore-stomach of fostered PY is immature and that the fore-stomsch maturation process has been accelerated by cross-fostering.

the milk composition and herbage consumed by fostered PY accelerate fore-stomach mucosal maturation by uncoupling the processes of down-regulating gastric glandular phenotype, and initiating cardia glandular development.
the milk from late lactation stage and/or herbage consumption by fostered PY may play an important role in regulating the transition of gastric to cardia phenotype in the wallaby PY fore-stomachs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
milk from later lactation stages accelerates fore-stoma maturation by down-regulating the gastric phenotype and that herbage consumed by fostered PY initiates the cardia glandular cell phenotype.
cross-fostering accelerates the transition from gastric to cardia gland phenotype, and that the timing of this transition is regulated by milk and herbage.
milk from later lactation stages and/or herbage are important in regulating the maturation of the fore-stomach during pouch life.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fore-stomachs of tammar wallaby PY are sensitive to changes in the milk they are fed, and that this can affect the timing of fore-stomatch maturation.
the fore-stomach of the tammar PY is responsive to changes in milk composition and diet.

the gastric glandular and cardia glandular phenotypes of the fore-stomach are regulated independently, and that the transition from gastric to cardia gland is regulated by the milk consumed by the PY.
